Exact numeric, Boolean and string values

Source: R/expressions.R
z3_int_val.Rd

Build Z3 values without going through floating point.

Usage

z3_int_val(ctx, value)

z3_real_val(ctx, value, den = NULL)

z3_bool_val(ctx, value)

z3_bv_val(ctx, value, width)

z3_string_val(ctx, value, escaped = FALSE)

z3_val(ctx, value, sort)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

value

The value; see Details.

den

For z3_real_val(), an optional denominator: a whole number, not zero.

width

Bit-vector width in bits.

escaped

For z3_string_val(), read value as an SMT-LIB string literal with \u{...} escapes.

sort

Target sort for z3_val().

Value

A z3_expr.

Details

z3_int_val() accepts a string of decimal digits with an optional sign, a whole number with absolute value at most 2^53, an R integer, or a gmp::bigz. z3_real_val() accepts an exact decimal ("0.125", "1.5e-3"), a fraction ("1/3", "-22/7"), an R number, or a gmp::bigq. Strings are parsed exactly, so z3_real_val(ctx, "0.1") is the rational 1/10. With den, z3_real_val(ctx, value, den) is the fraction value / den of two whole numbers (R integers, doubles of absolute value at most 2^53, or bit64::integer64 values), built without going through strings.

z3_string_val() converts an R string exactly, character by character. With escaped = TRUE it reads the string as an SMT-LIB string literal instead, so that \u{41} (written "\\u{41}" in R) is the character A; escapes beyond U+2FFFF or without a closing brace are kept as text. A raw vector gives one character per byte, with the code points 0 to 255 (so as.raw(0) is the character U+0000, which R strings cannot hold); bytes are not decoded as UTF-8. See z3_string_escaped() and z3_string_bytes() for the reverse conversions.

Converting R doubles

When an R number is combined with a Z3 expression, as in x + 0.1, it is converted as follows:

  • Whole numbers become exact integers. Whole numbers beyond 2^53 are rejected, because R may already have rounded them; pass them as strings or gmp::bigz instead.

  • Other finite doubles become the exact rational value of their shortest decimal representation that converts back to the same double, so 0.1 becomes 1/10 rather than the binary approximation 3602879701896397/36028797018963968. This matches what R prints.

  • NA, NaN and Inf are rejected.

Set options(z3r.doubles = "error") to reject non-integer doubles and require exact strings everywhere.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
z3_int_val(ctx, "123456789012345678901234567890")
#> <z3_expr Int> 123456789012345678901234567890
z3_real_val(ctx, "1/3")
#> <z3_expr Real> (/ 1.0 3.0)
z3_real_val(ctx, 1, 3)
#> <z3_expr Real> (/ 1.0 3.0)
z3_real_val(ctx, "0.125")
#> <z3_expr Real> (/ 1.0 8.0)
z3_bv_val(ctx, -1, 8)
#> <z3_expr (_ BitVec 8)> #xff
z3_string_val(ctx, "hello")
#> <z3_expr String> "hello"
z3_string_val(ctx, "tab\\u{9}", escaped = TRUE)
#> <z3_expr String> "tab\u{9}"
z3_string_val(ctx, as.raw(c(0x68, 0x69)))
#> <z3_expr String> "hi"
z3_val(ctx, 2, z3_real_sort(ctx))
#> <z3_expr Real> 2.0
